events.label: AMD Lisa Su keynote 9:30am PT (Day 2) + Intel Q2 AH — hardware confirmed, keynote adds hyperscaler wins
events.note: Lisa Su keynote at 9:30am PT / 12:30pm ET is the commercial partnership event following Day 1's hardware confirmations: EPYC Venice (first x86 2nm server CPU), MI455X in Helios rack with 31TB HBM4 at $5-5.5M pricing, and Microsoft Azure confirmed as H2 2026 anchor customer. Meta, OpenAI, xAI, Oracle, Cohere, and Red Hat were all present at Day 1 — keynote expected to add hyperscaler commitment announcements beyond Microsoft and deliver explicit Kimi K3 inference-economics counter-arguments. AMD closed +9.8% at $553 on Day 1 alone. Intel (INTC) Q2 AH: options imply 15% move; consensus $14.4B revenue / $0.22 non-GAAP EPS; enterprise semiconductor demand bellwether — guidance cut signals CapEx risk, guidance raise confirms AI demand thesis extends beyond hyperscalers. IBM also reports July 23 (94.4% historical beat rate, enterprise tech bellwether). Context: GOOGL Cloud +82% YoY beat sets a high bar for all AI-infrastructure reads; SPX 7,498.96 second qualifying close achieved; VIX 16.64 (first close below 17 formal trigger).

events.label: Kimi K3 full open-weight model weights public release — second AI narrative wave; 2.8T parameter model
events.note: Moonshot AI releases full Kimi K3 model weights (2.8 trillion parameters) publicly on July 27 — five days after GOOGL Q2 (Cloud +82%) and AMD Advancing AI Day 1 (MI455X/Helios confirmed shipping). Context has shifted since the prior briefing: GOOGL Cloud 82% growth is the strongest AI-demand confirmation on record, which reduces the likelihood that Kimi K3 efficiency arguments dominate the narrative. However, AMD Day 1's Helios at $5-5.5M and GOOGL's $195-205B capex commitment have refocused attention on the ROI question — and open-weight inference efficiency models (Kimi K3 at 70% pricing discount) directly challenge the hyperscaler inference-capex ROI thesis. Do not add NVDA or AMD into July 27 regardless of AMD keynote outcomes — Kimi K3 open weights are a known binary event risk on any GPU-exposed position.

events.label: FOMC meeting (Jul 28-29) — September hike probability 78%; most hawkish oil-inflation backdrop of the cycle
events.note: As of July 22 night: July hold probability ~83%; September hike probability ~78% — crossed the 70% formal BEARISH threshold (was 69% this morning, 48.7% two days ago) on WTI $86.85 and the structural oil pass-through risk from the Iran-US conflict. FOMC enters with WTI/Brent at crisis highs ($86.85/$94.13) and dual supply-shock (Hormuz restriction + Houthi Saudi maritime embargo) structurally active. The September language in the FOMC statement is the single most market-moving variable of the week: dovish September language = September hike probability collapses toward 50%, immediate rate-relief across IWM, TLT, and risk assets. Hawkish September language = probability jumps toward 85%+, extending the rate-shock regime through Q3. The FOMC must decide whether to acknowledge Brent $94.13 as a transitory or structurally embedding inflation signal — that language distinction moves all assets. Critical: any statement that does not explicitly close the door on September is read as hawkish given 78% market pricing.

events.label: META Q2 2026 earnings — AI cloud business quantification; MSFT Q2 + AMZN Q2 also; peak Q2 earnings week
events.note: META Q2 earnings July 29 is the first event requiring management to quantify the AI cloud business (Bloomberg July 1: Meta building AI cloud to sell excess compute). Context: GOOGL raised 2026 capex to $195-205B and committed to 2027 increases — META's AI cloud ambitions raise the same capex-ROI question. MSFT Azure must validate the AMD Helios deployment narrative with actual Azure AI revenue growth; AMD Day 1 confirmed MSFT as anchor customer, so MSFT must now show the revenue impact. AMZN AWS is the third major hyperscaler read on AI demand after GOOGL (82% growth). Also July 29: FOMC rate decision (4pm ET) — the rate decision plus three Mag-7 prints is the highest-density single session of Q2 season. A triple beat (META AI cloud revenue + MSFT Azure AI + AMZN AWS) alongside dovish FOMC September language is the single scenario that fully validates the upgrade cycle.

events.label: July CPI release (est. Aug 13) — WTI $86.85 + Brent $94.13 at crisis highs; most consequential macro print of 2026
events.note: July CPI is the first release to fully capture WTI at $86.85 and Brent at $94.13 — the crisis highs of the Iran-US conflict — amid the Hormuz blockade and Houthi maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia (~2.5M bbl/day at risk). September hike probability at 78% entering FOMC Jul 28-29 means the August CPI print directly determines whether September becomes near-certain or retreats. Bull scenario (July CPI ≤3.2% YoY with oil-shock not embedding in core): September hike probability collapses below 50%. Bear scenario (July CPI ≥3.5% YoY): September 50bps probability jumps toward 90%, BEARISH regime extends through Q4. Critical: WTI rose from ~$82 to $86.85 within a single session's oil shock (July 22 morning), and has remained elevated — August CPI captures the full Rubio 'not serious' escalation period. The GOOGL capex alarm ($195-205B) and TSLA margin miss (16.8%) are partly driven by the same cost-push inflation environment the August CPI will confirm or deny.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — $91B revenue guide; AI capex cycle clearing event; addresses Moonshot AI + TSMC wafer hike + AMD competition
events.note: NVDA's Q2 FY27 earnings is the fundamental clearing event for the AI capex thesis. $91B revenue guidance represents sequential acceleration. Context updated July 22: (1) AMD Day 1 confirmed MI455X in Helios rack with 31TB HBM4 shipping H2 2026 with Microsoft Azure anchor — AMD is now a confirmed NVDA competitor in the hyperscaler rack market, not just aspirational; (2) GOOGL raised 2026 capex to $195-205B and committed to a further increase in 2027 — the hyperscaler spend environment is extraordinary, which is a tailwind for NVDA; (3) TSMC wafer hike (5-10% on 2nm/3nm) affects both NVDA and AMD; (4) Kimi K3 open weights release July 27 will have occurred 30 days prior — demand impact must be quantified. The hard stop at $195 has held; do not add until post-Q2 FY27 print with all four risk factors (AMD competitive impact, Kimi K3 demand, TSMC wafer hike margin, capex ROI timeline) addressed in management guidance.

events.label: SPCX first earnings as a public company (approx.) — Starlink ARR + Starship cadence
events.note: First earnings print since June 12 IPO. SPCX touched an intraday all-time low of $132.75 on July 15 (below $135 IPO price) — down 30%+ from June 16 ATH of $225.64. 27 of 31 analysts still carry Buy ratings; the sell-side downgrade cycle has barely begun. December 2026 lock-up expiry adds supply overhang. Re-entry gate: first earnings print (Starlink ARR growth, Starship launch cadence, cash burn) is the fundamental clearing event. Net losses are structural ($4.9B in 2025, $4.28B in Q1 2026). Better entry $115-120 for risk-tolerant 12-month investors.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut, early investors and insiders can sell, materially expanding the ~4% public float. Lock-up expiries are a known supply overhang for hot IPOs. The $20B bond offering (June 22) already changed the capital structure risk profile — the lock-up expiry adds equity supply overhang.

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window shifts to H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). SoftBank sold off -13% on the delay. Microsoft and NVIDIA hold strategic stakes. The delay removes a near-term AI sentiment catalyst and adds uncertainty to AI infrastructure spending trajectories.
